one_line: Cheap because sales are still falling, China is shrinking and the new plan will take years. Brand and balance sheet are intact, so the fall is partly deserved.

why_fell.reason: Sales guidance was cut to a high single-digit fall for the full year
why_fell.evidence: Q1 FY27 sales fell 4% to $11.21B and missed estimates. Nike now expects the year to fall by a high single-digit percent. Adjusted profit guide is $1.15-$1.35 a share.

why_fell.reason: Investor day plan did not reassure the market
why_fell.evidence: Nike targets $5B extra sales and 12-14% operating margin by fiscal 2031, but only about 6% margin this year. Shares fell 6.3%. CEO said the turnaround will take longer than he would like.

why_fell.reason: Greater China and Converse are shrinking fast
why_fell.evidence: Greater China sales fell 22% (26% without currency effects) to $1.18B. Converse fell 28%. Nike is cutting thousands of online distributors in China from January.

why_fell.reason: Rivals are taking share and Morningstar cut its view of Nike's edge
why_fell.evidence: Morningstar lowered its moat rating and cut its profit estimate to $1.16 from $1.69. US sneaker share reportedly fell to 30% in 2025 from 40% in 2016. Seen in search summary only.

for_unfair.point: North America is growing again: sales up 2% to $5.13B, wholesale up 9%. Profit per share beat estimates (48 cents vs 43) and gross margin rose 0.6 points to 42.8%.
Tariffs may ease: Nike expects about $986M in refunds after the Supreme Court found the IEEPA tariffs were illegally collected. Only about $0.3B had been received by the June report.
Pace plan targets about $2.5B in savings by fiscal 2031. Management said gross margin growth would start in Q1 FY27, and it did. Morningstar still sees the stock as undervalued.

for_fair.point: Sales are falling and guidance is worse than before. Nike footwear fell 6% without currency effects in the August quarter, with units down 5%, while On grew 25% in Q3 2026.
for_fair.source: On Holding press release; Nike 10-Q via search summary

for_fair.point: Recovery is far off. Nike says declines ease only in fiscal 2028 and return to market growth in fiscal 2029. CFO said Nike must win back sneaker share, naming Adidas. Truist called recovery visibility limited.
Last year's profit was flattered by a one-time tariff refund (gross margin 49.2% reported, 40.2% without it). Tariffs stay a cost, and a 15% levy is assumed after July.

what_market_fears: That the brand has lost its edge to On, Hoka and Adidas, China keeps shrinking, and the five-year plan slips as earlier turnaround steps did.
what_would_prove_it_wrong: Total sales growth turning positive by fiscal 2028 as promised, with China and Converse stabilizing and North America growth holding. Another guidance cut or falling North America sales would show it is fair.
next_date_to_watch: Q2 FY27 earnings, expected around late December 2026 (date not confirmed in sources I read)

flag.note: Sales fell 4% last quarter and Nike guides a high single-digit fall for fiscal 2027, so the event is on track but the year is not finished.

not_found: Price check: Nike's last split was 2-for-1 in December 2015 and I found no 2026 split. A price near $36 is real; quotes in sources were about $38-$40 in Aug-Nov 2026 with a 52-week low near $32.
